where: iVUE account header — the working/billing number on the service order. Format is the 10-digit account string. 101, 125 = INT, 559 = Telephone
note: Trailing IN / OUT / QDS marks the direction of the order (IN = connect, OUT = disconnect).

where: LinePacks → the MGCP / endpoint name field. This is the full provisioning string for the voice port.
note: Reads as: office (FRNT) – cabinet/tech (PRSV_GPON) – shelf CLX01 – slot 01 – port 04 – etc.

where: LinePacks → the GR303 / endpoint name field. This is the full provisioning string for the voice port.
note: Taqua provisioning for voice agreements

where: LinePacks → Equipment, second column. The cabinet + card/slot/port identifier.
note: Second column on the equipment row — not the first.

where: LinePacks → Splitter view. Identifies the PON splitter shelf and port the customer rides.
note: S = splitter number, P = port number on that splitter.

where: iVUE → cable/pair record. The distribution cable + count/pair the service runs on.
note: Cable identifier followed by the pair/fiber count.

where: Fiberbook (or the as-built drawing) → MST and pedestal call-outs for the address.
note: Cross-check the as-built against Fiberbook when they disagree.

where: iVUE → Pedistal the home is fed from.

term: Parent Equipment — Internet line item / ONT SN
where: iVUE → parent equipment under the Internet line item → ONT serial / FSAN field.
note: Often blank until the ONT is registered — Warehouse or Diana in Customer Care will assign the ONT / Modem providing the serial number required for this field.

where: iVUE → service order header; the SO# (a related/grouped order may list several).
note: Multiple SO#s can appear when orders are bundled.

where: iVUE → order date; written at the head of the note in M.D.YY form.
note: Style JF writes it with slashes (8/1/23).

where: The work being done — summarized at the top of the note after the date.
note: Drives which workflow/variant applies.

where: FACS → after edits; record whether records were left alone, updated, or removed.
note: Common: No FACS Changed / FACS Updated / FACS Removed / FACS Cleared.

where: iVUE → the number being disconnected (the OUT line on a QDS swap).
note: (559)- Optional

where: iVUE → the number being connected (the IN line on a QDS swap).
note: (559)- Optional

where: QDS → the QDS-mapped number tied to the service swap.
note: Quick Dial Service for 911 - (559)- Optional

where: iVUE → billing account for the OUT number (101-prefixed).
note: Internet Account Number non tele prefix indicates internet

where: iVUE → billing account for the IN number (101-prefixed).
note: Internet Account Number non tele prefix indicates internet

where: The technician who wrote/completed the note; initials at the end of the date line.
note: Also your style selector -**- format (CT, JF, KM…).

where: LinePacks → the voice port string for the TEL section (switch-cabinet-shelf-slot-port + pair).
note: First token after *TEL.

where: LinePacks → First Column (Equipment) the data port string for the DSL section.
note: First token after *DSL.

where: LinePacks → any additional port not under TEL/DSL (cross-connect, secondary line).
FACS → the cable/pair + binding-post location for the TEL port.
note: BP = binding post.

where: FACS → the cable/pair + binding-post location for the DSL port.
note: BP = binding post.

where: The field-splicing instruction block in the note (PIC extend / spliced-through call-outs).
note: Flag for the splicer.

where: EDGE system → customer ID for EDGE FTTH product (always 125-001-XXXX).
iVUE → combined switch/cable/port assignment string.
note: Sometimes appears short (e.g. 328-1345).

where: LinePacks → the GPON upstream port for a fiber ONT.
note: FTTH only.

where: EDGE system → the FTTH downstream port + pair for EDGE service.
note: EDGE product only; rare.

where: Which monthly file the note came from. "… Line Assignments" = a Service Order; "… Tech Calls" = a trouble/tech-call note.
note: Tech Calls run longer and usually log a field correction.

where: The classified action pattern for the order (top workflow in the corpus).
note: Big buckets: DISC_QDS_RECON, VACA_RECONNECT, DISCONNECT_ONLY, UPGRADE_*, NPD.

where: On a tech-call note: the "Per <name>" tag crediting who directed the field change.
example: Per Bart, wound up using pr 1613 on cable 2
note: Frequent names: SE, Han, Kong, Tammie. Marks a same-SO correction, not a new order.

where: Tech-call language showing the originally-assigned port was changed in the field.
note: Signals BAD_PORT_UPDATE: the SO port did not work, FACS was updated to the real one.
